sections.title: Hol? or Hová?
sections.content: In unit 11 you said where someone *is*, with *-ban* or *-ben*: *a konyhában*. To say where someone is *going*, the place takes *-ba* or *-be* instead: *a konyhába*. It is the same ending with the final *-n* dropped. *Hol?* (“where?”) goes with *-ban/-ben*, and *Hová?* (“where to?”) goes with *-ba/-be*. The verb for going is *megy*; the next screen has it.

sections.title: Which ending?
sections.content: The vowel rule has not changed. A word with a back vowel takes *-ba*: *bolt* becomes *boltba*. A word with only front vowels takes *-be*: *kert* becomes *kertbe*. The vowels *i* and *í* are neutral. A final *-a* or *-e* grows long as the ending is added: *szoba* becomes *szobába*, *iskola* becomes *iskolába*, with *á*. The final *-i* of *nappali* does not change: *nappaliba*.

sections.title: Place, and going to the place

items.english: I am going to the kitchen.
Anna is going to the shop.
Dad is going to the garden.

sections.content: Compare *a konyhában* (“in the kitchen”) with *a konyhába* (“into the kitchen”). Only the last letter differs, but the meaning changes from staying to going. Keep the accent on the lengthened vowel: *szobába* is right, *szobaba* is a misspelling.
